# Lorenzo's Blog

> Personal blog — Kubernetes, homelab, AI infrastructure, monitoring, and self-hosting by Lorenzo Girardi.

This file follows the llms.txt convention (https://llmstxt.org). Each post is also available as clean Markdown by appending `index.md` to its URL. A full-text dump of every post is at https://www.k8s.it/llms-full.txt.

## Posts

- [The Safe Zone: Where AI Actually Belongs in Business Processes](https://www.k8s.it/posts/the-safe-zone-where-ai-actually-belongs-in-business-processes/): A framework for finding AI's real use cases in business processes, backed by a production case study: an Algolia usage exporter built in 4 hours.
- [I Made Claude Code Talk Like a Caveman for 61 Days, Then Did the Math](https://www.k8s.it/posts/i-made-claude-code-talk-like-a-caveman-for-61-days-then-did-the-math/): I mined 27 Claude Code session logs to measure what caveman-mode token compression actually saves in API dollars, and found the real cost was hiding somewhere caveman mode can't touch.
- [Who Is Your AI Agent Acting For? RFC 8693 On-Behalf-Of Delegation](https://www.k8s.it/posts/who-is-your-ai-agent-acting-for-rfc-8693-on-behalf-of-delegation/): How I built a local POC where every LLM and MCP call carries both   the human's and the agent's identity, using Keycloak and RFC 8693 token   exchange. Per-user policy, audit and revocation for autonomous agents.
- [Running a Local LLM on AMD Radeon 780M — gfx1103, ROCm, and the GPU That Wasn't Supposed to Work](https://www.k8s.it/posts/running-a-local-llm-on-amd-radeon-780m-gfx1103-rocm-and-the-gpu-that-wasnt-supposed-to-work/): A full walkthrough of setting up Gemma 4 12B QAT on a Lenovo M75Q Gen5 mini-PC with AMD Radeon 780M iGPU. ROCm kernel mapping, GTT memory, GPU clock optimization, and a surprising benchmark result: CPU beats GPU on generation speed.
- [AI Agentic Development Changes Who Builds Software — and That's an Infrastructure Problem](https://www.k8s.it/posts/ai-agentic-development-changes-who-builds-software-and-thats-an-infrastructure-problem/): Agentic AI tools let non-technical people build working apps. That's great. Where do those apps go? A deep dive into building a safe, self-contained Kubernetes environment with an explicit platform contract for vibe-coded applications.
- [Monitoring Contentful Usage — Building a Prometheus Exporter Because the UI Won't Tell You](https://www.k8s.it/posts/monitoring-contentful-usage-with-a-prometheus-exporter/): How I built a read-only Prometheus exporter for Contentful usage metrics, deployed it on Kubernetes, and finally got visibility into API consumption across spaces and orgs.
- [Algolia prometheus exporter ](https://www.k8s.it/posts/algolia-prometheus-exporter/): Algolia Usage Exporter — A Case Study in AI-Assisted Tooling What is this? A lightweight Prometheus exporter that collects usage and infrastructure metrics from the Algolia search API and exposes them at /metrics for Prometheus / Datadog scraping. It runs as a standalone HTTP server (single binary via Docker/Podman), requires minimal configuration (just two API keys), and exports metrics like: Usage statistics: search operations, records, processing time, QPS, write operations Infrastructure metrics: CPU, RAM, SSD utilization, build times (Premium plan only) Health signals: scrape success status, timestamps The entire project lives in a single Python package with ~50KB of code, a Helm chart for Kubernetes deployment, and full test coverage across unit, integration, and e2e layers.
- [Stargate LLM Gateway](https://www.k8s.it/posts/stargate-llm-gateway/): Stargate LLM Gateway OpenAI-compatible LLM Gateway for AWS Bedrock with user management, usage tracking, and cost monitoring. Powered by LiteLLM. - [Redefining E-commerce for the Age of Conversational AI](https://www.k8s.it/posts/redefining-ux-for-the-age-of-conversational-ai/): How JSON-LD and structured data transform e-commerce for AI-driven discovery — a hands-on case study with demo-app-eshop.
- [Migrating Homelab from VMware ESXi to Proxmox: A New Era](https://www.k8s.it/posts/migrating-homelab-from-vmware-esxi-to-proxmox-a-new-era/): How Broadcom's acquisition of VMware pushed me to migrate my homelab to Proxmox — hardware choices, migration strategy, and what I gained.
- [Building a Scalable Image CDN with MinIO, imgproxy, and Cloudflare](https://www.k8s.it/posts/building-a-scalable-image-cdn-with-minio-imgproxy-and-cloudflare/): How to build a self-hosted image CDN using MinIO for storage, imgproxy for on-the-fly resizing, and Cloudflare for edge caching — deployed on Kubernetes.
- [Websocket, Cloudflare Tunnel, Apache httpd and a Bit of Security](https://www.k8s.it/posts/websocket-cloudflare-tunnel-apache-and-irritation/): How I built a secure homelab ingress using Cloudflare Tunnel, Apache HTTPD, and Kubernetes — with WebSocket support for Grafana and zero open ports.
- [HPA vs Rate-limit](https://www.k8s.it/posts/hpa-vs-rate-limit/): A hands-on lab comparing Horizontal Pod Autoscaling and rate limiting in Kubernetes — load tests with Gatling to find the optimal configuration for a CPU-bound Python service.
- [Application Rate Limit](https://www.k8s.it/posts/application-rate-limiting/): Two ways to implement rate limiting for your application: embedding it in the code vs running it in a sidecar container with Envoy.
- [YA VPN Service in Kubernetes](https://www.k8s.it/posts/ya-vpn-service-in-kubernetes/): Moving from strongswan IPsec to WireGuard in Kubernetes — key generation, deployment, and a Prometheus exporter sidecar for monitoring.
- [Lazy People Do It Better](https://www.k8s.it/posts/lazy-people-do-it-better/): Why HPA with KEDA and Prometheus metrics beats manual scaling — testing autoscaling with Gatling load tests against a Python Fibonacci API.
- [Kubernetes nstats](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-nstats/): A sidecar container to monitor pod-level network traffic with iftop, awk, Python, and InfluxDB — because knowing IN/OUT is not enough.
- [Homelab, When Small is Big](https://www.k8s.it/posts/homelab-when-small-is-big/): Building a silent, cheap, 24/7 homelab on an Intel NUC with VMware ESXi, ghettoVCB backups, and everything needed to run Kubernetes at home.
- [Ambient Sensor for Mere Mortal](https://www.k8s.it/posts/ambient-sensor-for-mere-mortal/): Building a temperature and humidity sensor with ESP8266, DHT22, and Lua — shipping metrics to InfluxDB and visualizing them in Grafana for under $5.
- [The Monitoring Paper](https://www.k8s.it/posts/the-monitoring-paper/): A framework for monitoring that actually matters: System, Application, and Business metrics — and why buying a tool won't solve your observability problem.
- [Maximum Yield with Minimum Expense](https://www.k8s.it/posts/maximum-yield-with-minimum-expense/): How to run a static website with Minio on Kubernetes, secure it with Cloudflare Workers security headers, and monitor it — keeping it simple and safe.
- [Kubernetes Destroyed the Virtualization... or NOT](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-destroyed-the-virtualization-or-not/): Why Kubernetes and virtualization are not antagonists — the case for running Kubernetes on VMs and why major cloud providers agree.
- [Kubernetes API Gateway](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-apigw/): Setting up Kong as an API gateway in Kubernetes with rate limiting per user, key authentication, Konga admin UI, and Cloudflare WAF protection.
- [Python REST API Test Application](https://www.k8s.it/posts/python-rest-api-test-application/): A simple Python Flask REST API built for platform testing — deployable locally with Docker or in Kubernetes with wildcard DNS ingress routing.
- [Kubernetes sitespeed.io](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-sitespeedio/): Running sitespeed.io as a Kubernetes CronJob with Argo Workflows to get objective website performance metrics from the customer's perspective.
- [Kubernetes Postfix](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-postfix/): Migrating Postfix with OpenDKIM from a $1 VPS to Kubernetes — ConfigMaps, Secrets, and a Dockerfile that bundles everything in one container.
- [Kubernetes VPN Strongswan — IPsec with LDAP Auth](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-strongswan/): Running Strongswan IPsec-XAuth VPN in Kubernetes with LDAP authentication — no credential files, no redeployment for user changes, enterprise-grade access control.
- [Kubernetes Service Mesh](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-servicemesh/): Do we actually need a service mesh? An honest evaluation of what it is, what it isn't, when it adds value, and a hands-on lab with Cilium and Istio.
- [Kubernetes Guacamole — Bastion Host Without MySQL](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-guacamole/): Running Apache Guacamole in Kubernetes as a lightweight bastion host, using user-mapping.xml via ConfigMap instead of MySQL — simpler, scalable, Kubernetes-native.
- [Kubernetes Apache HTTPD — The Front Controller Pattern](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-apacherr/): Why Apache HTTPD still has a place in Kubernetes as a front controller — managing complex routing, A/B testing, and multi-country path resolution for large e-commerce sites.
- [Docker-latency — The Network Blaming Tool](https://www.k8s.it/posts/docker-latency/): A Docker Compose Grafana stack for monitoring internet latency and packet loss — built to answer the eternal question: is it the VPN, or is it you?
- [Terraform Your Free Cloudflare Account](https://www.k8s.it/posts/terraform-your-free-cloudflare-account/): How to manage your entire Cloudflare DNS, WAF, and zone settings as infrastructure-as-code using Terraform and GitLab CI.
- [Kubernetes for Mere Mortals](https://www.k8s.it/posts/kubernetes-for-mere-mortals/): Building a homemade Kubernetes cluster on ARM OrangePi hardware — from zero to running pods with Traefik ingress and Grafana monitoring.
